title: How a Simple Latch Secures a Door ⚙️
topic: How does a simple latch keep a door closed?
topic_key: closed door keep latch simple

facts.intro: A door latch uses a simple lever‑and‑slider mechanism to lock and unlock a door without any electricity or fluid.
facts.reveal: The lever (handle) pivots around a pin, while the slider (bolt) slides horizontally to engage the door frame.
facts.step1: At beat 1 the handle is pulled down, rotating the lever clockwise about its pin.
facts.step2: The lever’s rotation is coupled to the bolt with a 1:‑1 ratio, pulling the bolt outward.
facts.step3: The spring attached to the bolt stores energy, keeping the bolt extended when the handle is released.
facts.step4: At beat 3 the handle returns to neutral, allowing the spring to pull the bolt back into the locked position.
facts.hold: The bolt stays engaged by the spring’s force until the handle is pulled again.
facts.payoff: This demonstrates how a mechanical latch can securely hold a door closed using only levers, sliders, and springs.

title: How a Simple Soap Dispenser Works ⚙️
topic: How does a manual soap dispenser pump?
topic_key: dispenser manual pump soap

facts.intro: A user squeezes the handle, turning the cam attached to it.
facts.reveal: The cam’s eccentric shape pushes the plunger upward as it rotates.
facts.step1: When the plunger rises, it opens a small valve at the bottom of the bottle.
facts.step2: Soap is drawn up through the valve into the plunger chamber.
facts.step3: Continued rotation lifts the plunger further, compressing the spring.
facts.step4: At the peak of the lift, the valve closes and the spring forces the plunger down.
facts.hold: The downward stroke forces the soap out through the nozzle.
facts.payoff: Releasing the handle lets the cam reset, and the spring returns the plunger ready for the next squeeze.

title: How a Hand Crank Freezes Ice Cream ⚙️
topic: How does a manual ice cream maker work
topic_key: cream ice maker manual

recipe.title: How a manual ice cream maker works

facts.intro: You see a hand crank on the side of the freezer bowl, connected to a small rotating cam.
facts.reveal: The cam has a raised lobe that pushes up on a vertical plunger as it turns.
facts.step1: When the cam lifts, the plunger pushes the paddle down through the frozen mixture, breaking ice crystals.
facts.step2: The paddle’s motion is visible as it churns the creamy base while the cam continues to rotate.
facts.step3: As the cam lobe passes, the spring attached to the plunger pulls it back up, resetting for the next stroke.
facts.step4: Each crank rotation repeats the lift‑push‑release cycle, gradually turning the mixture into smooth ice cream.
facts.hold: The spring’s tension keeps the plunger ready to be lifted again without manual effort.
facts.payoff: After many rotations, the continuous cam‑press action transforms the liquid into frozen ice cream.

title: Why a garden sprayer makes fine mist ⚙️
topic: Why does a garden sprayer spray a fine mist?
topic_key: fine garden mist spray sprayer

facts.intro: A clear tank holds the blue‑tinged liquid, showing the amount remaining as the sprayer is used.
facts.reveal: Pressing the thumb lever pulls the pump plunger back, compressing the return spring inside the barrel.
facts.step1: When the lever is released, the spring pushes the plunger forward, closing the valve at the top of the tank.
facts.step2: The forward motion forces a small amount of liquid up through the internal tube toward the mist nozzle.
facts.step3: At the nozzle, the liquid meets a tiny aperture that atomizes it into a fine mist as it exits.
facts.step4: The mist stream shoots out of the spout, coating plants evenly while the tank gradually empties.
facts.hold: If the trigger is held down, the spring continues to drive the plunger, delivering a steady stream until the tank empties.
facts.payoff: Releasing the trigger lets the spring reset, readying the sprayer for the next precise burst of mist.
